title: Estate Claim Documentation Terms — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital)
content:
# Estate Claim Documentation Terms

These terms apply to an estate's application to have a deceased member's Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) retired. They are identical in the Residential, Seasonal, Farm, General Service, Irrigation and Large Power Patron Classes.

| Term | Value in every patron class |
|---|---|
| Window for submitting an estate application | 36 calendar months after the date of death |
| Documents that must be on file for the application to be complete | certified death certificate; authority document; the estate's IRS Form W-9 |
| Estate's IRS Form W-9 on file before payment | Required |
| Documents accepted as proof of the claimant's authority | letters testamentary; letters of administration; small estate affidavit |
| Largest payout made on a small estate affidavit instead of letters testamentary or letters of administration | $25000.00 |
| When complete estate applications are approved | at the monthly board meeting, held on the third Tuesday |

## Terms explained

- The **authority document** is the paper that names the claimant as the person with authority over the deceased member's estate; only the three kinds listed are accepted.
- A **small estate affidavit** serves as the authority document only for a payout of at most $25000.00. For a larger payout, letters testamentary or letters of administration are the accepted documents.
- The **36-month window** runs from the member's date of death.

## Hypothetical illustrations

| Authority document on file | Payout | Accepted as authority |
|---|---|---|
| small estate affidavit | $24999.99 | Yes |
| small estate affidavit | $25000.00 | Yes |
| small estate affidavit | $25000.01 | No |
| letters of administration | any amount | Yes |
